candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Contact Precautions PPE
candidate.educational_objective: For Contact Precautions, don the indicated gown and gloves upon room entry for anticipated patient or environmental contact and remove/discard contaminated PPE before leaving the room.

options.A: Don a gown and gloves on room entry for interactions that may involve contact with the client or the client's environment, and discard contaminated PPE before leaving the room.
options.B: Wear only a surgical mask on room entry because Contact Precautions are designed primarily for respiratory-droplet exposure.
options.C: Use a fit-tested N95 respirator as the required PPE for every Contact Precautions interaction, even when no airborne pathogen is suspected.
options.D: Enter without gown or gloves and add PPE only after visible contamination occurs during care.

candidate.rationale: CDC Contact Precautions guidance directs healthcare personnel to use gloves and a gown for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment, with PPE donned upon room entry and contaminated PPE discarded before exiting. Therefore A is correct. B describes a droplet-focused barrier, C applies an airborne respirator requirement to Contact Precautions, and D delays PPE until after exposure rather than using it prospectively for anticipated contact.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC Contact Precautions include gown and gloves for interactions involving patient or environmental contact, donned on room entry and discarded before exit; masks and N95 respirators are specified under different transmission-based precaution categories.
